L402: ## 8.6 API keys — who needs what L403: L404: There are **two entirely separate LLM roles**; they never share a key, and the end user supplies nothing. L405: | | **Pipeline LLM** (Gemini Flash) | **Consumption LLM** | L406: |---|---|---| L407: | Job | extract claims, reconcile | answer the user's question in-agent | L408: | Runs in | *maintainer's* GitHub Actions, daily | the *user's* Claude Code / Codex | L409: | Key provided by | **maintainer** — one Gemini key as a repo GitHub Secret | **nobody** — the user's existing agent | L410: | Cost borne by | free tier (maintainer account) | the user's existing subscription | L411: **The MCP server makes zero LLM calls of its own.** By the time a user queries OpenPitch, extraction/reconciliation already ran centrally and was committed as plain JSON; the server is a dumb data reader, and the "intelligence" at query time is the **user's own agent** reasoning over pre-computed data. L412: ``` L413: MAINTAINER (once/day, central) USER (on demand, local) L414: GitHub Action → Gemini extracts git Claude Code/Codex asks → MCP reads L415: → commits clean JSON ──────────────────▶ JSON → user's agent phrases answer L416: ↑ Gemini key lives here ONLY ↑ NO key, NO Gemini, NO LLM call by MCP L417: ``` L418: **End-user install = add the MCP server to config. No signup, no key, no cost.** L419: The *only* party needing a Gemini key is the maintainer (or an advanced user who forks and self-hosts their own daily pipeline instead of consuming the published data). This is documented prominently in the README. L420: ## 8.7 A2A (agent-to-agent) interface — OpenPitch as a delegate agent L421: L422: MCP exposes OpenPitch as a **tool**; A2A exposes it as an **agent** other agents can discover and delegate to (BRD §4.1.6). The two are **complementary** (MCP = vertical tool access; A2A = horizontal agent coordination), which is the emerging default for agent systems. L423: - **Agent Card** (`/.well-known/agent.json`) advertising OpenPitch's skills, e.g. `research_company`, `compare_companies`, `whats_moved`, `find_contradictions`. L424: - A thin A2A server wraps the **same read layer** the MCP server uses (the git-tracked data) — no new data path, and still **zero LLM calls of its own** for pure-data skills. L425: - Hostable as a static Agent Card + a lightweight endpoint; for the fully-static/zero-cost posture, the Agent Card + JSON feed can satisfy discovery and simple delegation, with a richer hosted A2A endpoint as an optional add-on. L426: This turns OpenPitch from "a data source you query" into "a specialist agent your agent hires" — and is, to our knowledge, the first **free, open A2A startup-intelligence agent**. Implemented behind the same data contract, so MCP and A2A never diverge. L427: ## 8.8 Ease of implementation (a first-class design goal — BRD pillar 1) L428: L429: Frictionless adoption is an explicit requirement (BR-25), not a nicety. Target: **working in an agent in <60s, no key, no signup.** Surfaces, cheapest-first: L430: | Surface | Effort for adopter | L431: |---|---| L432: | MCP server | one line in agent config (`uvx openpitch-mcp`) | L433: | A2A agent | point an agent at the Agent Card URL | L434: | Raw JSON | fetch `data/companies/*.json` from raw GitHub | L435: | RSS/Atom events | subscribe — works with no-code tools | L436: L437: A measured **<60s "first answer"** is tracked as a product metric; the README leads with a GIF proving it. L438: ## 9. Dashboard (secondary interface) L439: L440: Static site built from the same JSON, deployed to GitHub Pages (BRD §4.1.3). Two views: L441: - **Overview** — sortable grid of all 50 × key metrics; default sort is valuation, with controls for total funding, source coverage, category, and name. L442: - **Detail (on select)** — full metric panel, per-metric history chart, provenance + confidence per figure, contradiction badges. L443: Built in stage 7; no runtime backend.
